input.quote: 7.2 Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.
input.rationale: Section 7.2 imposes an MFN obligation on us (Customer), not on Vendor: we would have to extend Silverline the best terms we give any other technology supplier. It is unqualified as to product, duration, and comparability, which is the playbook walk-away position (open-ended obligation to extend Vendor any better terms given to a third party). The preferred position is no MFN burdening Customer, so we delete the clause; MFN pricing in our favour would remain welcome. Deletion also resolves the duplicate "7.2" numbering with the invoicing clause at p0028.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We deleted the open-ended obligation for us to extend Vendor the best terms we give any other technology supplier, as we do not accept MFN obligations running against the Customer. An MFN in our favour remains welcome; if Vendor needs something here, we could consider a narrow MFN limited to a defined product for 12 months with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
proposal.summary: Delete Customer-side MFN obligation in Section 7.2.
